significance: The principal temple of Amarkantak, standing at the source of the Narmada, built by the Kalachuris of Tripuri in the 12th century and later renovated by Maharani Ahilyabai Holkar. Amarkantak, where three major rivers rise, is described in Hindu scripture as the king of pilgrimages.
story: Adi Shankaracharya is said to have settled the dispute over the river's true source by declaring the stream at the temple to be the Narmada's mainstream.
